rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data yet, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five line sensors spread across the 80 mm sensor span (x = -0.04 to +0.04 m, step 0.02 m) at y = 0.05 m ahead of the axle, so the robot sees the line well before the wheels reach it. The 12 mm footprint is wider than the 8 mm option, so the line is seen across the full 25 mm tape width and readings change smoothly. Wheel track 0.12 m and wheel radius 0.03 m give moderate turn authority. Mass 0.8 kg and body 0.12 x 0.16 m keep yaw inertia low enough for quick corrections while the off-track limit stays comfortable at about 0.06 m. Controller: sensor weights -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 make the signal sign match the contract (positive = left, so a tape reading on the left sensors steers left). kp = 2.0 gives a strong proportional response; kd = 0.3 damps the swing without adding much jitter; ki = 0 avoids integral windup on curves. base_speed = 1.6 is a compromise: it should be near the 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s, but high enough to risk overshooting the tighter bends. line_loss = last_direction so the robot recovers toward the side it was last on. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some risk on the slalom. The main unknowns are the speed-versus-off-track trade-off and whether kp is too high, which the race telemetry (rms_error, max_error, steering_oscillation, completion_time) should reveal. Next measurements: whether lateral error stays under 0.03 m on bends, and whether the robot finishes before 3.0 s.
